theme: GnIES against gnies 0.3.3, the authors' package; UT-IGSP against graphical-model-learning 0.1a8, the authors' library; IGSP against graphical-model-learning 0.1a8, the authors' library, and a copy of it patched to Definition 4.2; ICP against InvariantCausalPrediction, in and out of the claim; DYNOTEARS against CausalNex 0.12.2, the authors' implementation; CAM-UV against lingam 1.13.0 and causal-learn 0.1.4.8
build: GnIES: Andrey pre-release build of 3 November 2026 (version string 0.13.0) for every fit but the order check, which ran on a build of the same day that adds DEBUG records of the steps a tie decided; with the records off, its GIES and GES outputs equal the first build's | UT-IGSP: Andrey pre-release build of 3 November 2026 (version string 0.13.0) for Andrey's fits; the reference's fits ran in an earlier job on the same data, which the build regenerated identically | IGSP: Andrey pre-release build of 3 November 2026 (version string 0.13.0) for every in-claim and out-of-claim fit | ICP: pre-release Andrey 0.14.0 build, 3 November 2026 | DYNOTEARS: Andrey pre-release builds: the 0.13.0 branch of 31 October 2026 for the Gaussian, centered exponential, Barabasi-Albert, and out-of-claim settings, and the 0.14.0 branch of 3 November 2026 for the exponential noise of mean 1 and the Barabasi-Albert graphs at 50 steps; refitted on the 0.14.0 build, every recorded Andrey fit up to 50 variables and 20 at 100 variables return the same graph (identity) | CAM-UV: Andrey pre-release build of the 0.13.0 branch, 1 November 2026; andrey.camuv's source is the same in every commit of that branch from 12e380fc9, which adds CAM-UV, to 7d85ce6d5, the branch's tip that day. The fits on seeds 20-39 with one node in five hidden at d = 10 and on seeds 10-19 with nothing hidden ran on a pre-release build of the 0.14.0 branch, 3 November 2026, whose andrey.camuv code is the same and whose column ranks, the order the sets are visited in, are the same on every dataset of the lane
verdict_rule: GnIES: per cell and per metric (shd, target_error), D = error(Andrey at its defaults) - error(gnies at its defaults) per dataset, on datasets both finished and the model check passed; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs is reported, not judged. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, the generator seeded by the CRC-32 of '<cell>/<metric>/<comparison>'. A worse cell counts only if its rerun on seeds 20-39 is worse too; a better cell is cited only if its rerun is better too. Out-of-claim cells are reported and never judged. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | UT-IGSP: per cell, row, and metric (shd, target_error): D = error(Andrey) - error(reference) per dataset, each the mean over 5 draws; side = where the 95% percentile bootstrap interval of mean D (10,000 resamples) lies; worse = above 0 on seeds 0-19 and on the rerun on seeds 2000-2019; better = below 0 on seeds 0-19 and on the rerun on seeds 2000-2019, seeds that played no part in choosing the default; otherwise the row is named by its side on seeds 0-19 and 'not replicated', or 'tie'. The confirmation's seeds 4000-4019 are those on which J2's default was chosen, as the setting with the most rows below 0 there, so they are not an independent replication and decide no verdict: 17 more J2 rows were lower on seeds 0-19 and on seeds 4000-4019, the seeds that chose the default. In a row, multi_draw holds the interval on seeds 0-19, side its side, replication the rerun on seeds 2000-2019, confirmation the rerun on seeds 4000-4019, and verdict the result; out of claim, verdict is the side. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | IGSP: per cell, row, level, and comparator: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(reference) per dataset, each the mean over 5 draws; side = where the 95% percentile bootstrap interval of mean D lies, read exactly (an end within 1e-12 of 0, floating-point residue of an exact 0, is read as 0; the gate read the ends as computed); worse = above 0 on seeds 0-19 and on a rerun on fresh seeds 100-119; better = below 0 on seeds 0-19 and on a rerun on fresh seeds (100-119, or 6000-6019 for J2 at alpha 1e-3); a row is judged only where the library beats the empty graph. In a row, multi_draw holds the interval on seeds 0-19, side its side, replication the rerun on seeds 100-119, confirmation the rerun on seeds 6000-6019 (at alpha 1e-3, 10 starts), default igsp at its default level on those seeds against the comparator at alpha 1e-3 (the default's evidence, one seed set, so its side is not a verdict), and verdict the result; out of claim, verdict is the side. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | ICP: D = error(Andrey) - error(InvariantCausalPrediction) per paired fit; worse when the paired 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | DYNOTEARS: D = SHD(Andrey) - SHD(CausalNex) per series on the series both finished; the mean D with its percentile bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples); a setting in claim with at least 10 pairs is worse when the interval lies above 0, better when below, a tie otherwise; a worse setting is run again on 20 fresh seeds (20-39, the replication in its row) and counts as worse only if the replication's interval also lies above 0; a better setting is run again the same way and counts as better only if its replication's interval also lies below 0. Settings with claim 'out' are reported, not judged. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there | CAM-UV: D = direct_errors(Andrey) - direct_errors(reference) per dataset on the datasets both finished, for each of lingam and causal-learn at the paper's set size and lingam at its default; the mean D with its percentile bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples); a cell in claim is worse when the interval lies above 0, better when below, a tie otherwise; a cell worse or better is run again on 20 fresh seeds (20-39, the replication rows) and keeps its verdict only if the replication's interval lies on the same side of 0 (final_verdict). Cells with claim 'out' are reported, not judged. Floor, in every row that records one (floor): andrey_minus_empty is the 95% interval of the mean of Andrey's error minus the empty estimate's (the empty graph, or for a target error the given targets alone, or no targets), and reference_minus_empty the same for the reference; the floor applies only where the reference's interval lies wholly below 0, where the reference itself beats the empty estimate, and there Andrey's interval must lie wholly below 0 too; elsewhere it is reported as not applied (applies false), with its numbers. The floor is judged on the first seeds; a replication's floor (the rerun on fresh seeds) only confirms a failure there
card_verdict_rule: card_verdict, on every row: the release card's verdict on the row's comparison, 'better', 'tie', or 'worse', and null where the card judges none (rows out of claim, UT-IGSP at the paper's level, IGSP at its other levels and starts, and ICP's speed rows). Better or worse counts only where a rerun on fresh seeds agreed; one on the first seeds alone is a tie, and so are the 17 UT-IGSP rows below 0 on seeds 0-19 and on the seeds that chose the default, 4000-4019, which are not fresh. CAM-UV is judged against each of its three references. IGSP's rows at alpha 1e-3 and 10 starts carry the card's verdict at Andrey's defaults (the row's default, seeds 6000-6019), against the library and against its Definition 4.2 copy; better or worse only at 1,000 rows, where the row's side on seeds 0-19 agreed. ICP's card judges a regime over all its sizes, so each of the regime's rows carries that verdict.
fit_protocol: GnIES: every arm of a dataset back to back on one pinned core with one BLAS thread; a cap of 1,800 s per fit at 10 variables (300 s for gnies with the true targets fixed) and 3,600 s on the variable ladder; a fit past its cap is a timeout, never an empty graph; a gnies fit whose total is not finite or whose local scores returned NaN is an error and leaves its cell's pairs | UT-IGSP: every package of a dataset in its own child process pinned to one core with one BLAS thread; 5 draws per dataset in claim (Andrey seed 0-4, the library's Python random and NumPy global generator seeded 0-4), one out of claim; a cap of 1,800 s per draw (3,600 s at 100 variables and with kernel tests), a timeout never scored | IGSP: every package of a dataset in its own child process pinned to one core with one BLAS thread; 5 draws per dataset in claim (Andrey seed 0-4, the library's Python random and NumPy global generator seeded 0-4), one out of claim; a cap of 1,800 s per draw in claim and 3,600 s out of it, a draw over it a timeout, never scored | ICP: every fit on 1 core, 4 at a time, no wall cap; Andrey's speed rows are the median of 3 timed fits after one untimed one, the others one fit; R's time covers its ICP() call alone | DYNOTEARS: one timed fit per series, no warm-up, one BLAS thread on one core, four fits at a time on four cores, a 3600 s wall cap per fit; andrey_cpu_s and comparator_cpu_s are the medians of the fits' CPU time, cpu_ratio the median over the paired series of CausalNex's CPU time over Andrey's, with its bootstrap 95% interval | CAM-UV: one timed fit per dataset, no warm-up, one BLAS thread on one core, four fits at a time on four cores, a 3600 s wall cap per fit; *_cpu_s are the medians of the fits' CPU time, cpu_ratio the median over the paired datasets of the reference's CPU time over Andrey's, with its bootstrap 95% interval. lingam at its default set size (lingam_default) ran on the same stored datasets in runs of its own, two days after the others, so its cpu_ratio pairs fits from different runs
error_metric: GnIES: each entry's own, in its error_metric and metric: the SHD of the interventional essential graph or the target error, as the median over the paired datasets (the _mean fields hold the means) | UT-IGSP: each entry's own, in its error_metric and metric: the SHD of the interventional essential graph or the target error, as the median over the paired datasets of each dataset's mean over its draws (the _mean fields hold the means) | IGSP: SHD of the interventional essential graph, as the median over the paired datasets of each dataset's mean over its draws (the _mean fields hold the means) | ICP: each entry's own, in its error_metric | DYNOTEARS: each entry's own, in its error_metric: the edge SHD over the window, as the mean over the paired series | CAM-UV: each entry's own, in its error_metric: the direct-edge errors (direct_errors), as the mean over the paired datasets
complete_definition: GnIES: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored | UT-IGSP: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored | IGSP: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored | ICP: true when every planned fit finished; no fit timed out | DYNOTEARS: true when every setting has at least 10 paired series (both packages finished); no fit reached its cap | CAM-UV: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (every package finished); no fit reached its cap
seeds_note: GnIES: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting: 20 (seeds 0-19) in every in-claim and out-of-claim setting at 10 variables, with reruns on seeds 20-39 in the replication of the 7 settings that came out better; 10 (seeds 0-9) on the ladder of 20 to 100 variables, where the reference ran 10 seeds at 20 variables, 3 at 30, and none at 50 and 100 | UT-IGSP: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting: 20 (seeds 0-19), 10 (seeds 0-9) at 50 and 100 variables; 5 draws per dataset in claim, 1 out of claim; reruns on seeds 2000-2019 in the 11 in-claim cells with a comparison above 0 in the first comparison, and, at the defaults, the confirmation's seeds 4000-4019 in every in-claim cell. Categorical data (Andrey alone) is in the lane file only | IGSP: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting: 20 (seeds 0-19), 10 (seeds 0-9) at 50 and 100 variables; 5 draws per dataset in claim, 1 out of claim; reruns on seeds 100-119 in the 7 in-claim cells with a comparison above 0 on seeds 0-19, and, at alpha 1e-3 with 10 starts, the confirmation's seeds 6000-6019 in every in-claim cell. Categorical data (Andrey alone) and 200 and 400 variables (no library run) are in the lane file only | ICP: scenario seeds [658, cell, scenario] and dataset seeds [658, cell, scenario, dataset], as benchmarks/icp_cpu.py draws them; a row's seeds counts its paired datasets, the datasets of its scenarios that both packages fit, and the cell B rows hold the first 20 datasets of each scenario whose intervened set holds the target | DYNOTEARS: 20 series per setting in claim (seeds 0-19), 10 per setting out of claim (seeds 0-9); replications on seeds 20-39 of every setting judged worse or better | CAM-UV: 20 datasets per cell in claim (seeds 0-19), 10 per cell out of claim (seeds 0-9), and replications on seeds 20-39: the paper's simulation at both sizes and one node in five hidden at d = 10, and nothing hidden on seeds 0-19; a seed whose graph cannot hide its nodes is skipped and the next one taken: seed 31 at d = 10 with one node in five hidden, so that replication reads seeds 20-30 and 32-40
residue_note: UT-IGSP: a side is read after rounding the interval's ends to 10 decimals: three ends are floating-point residue of an exact 0 (5e-18 and -6e-18 in the final rows J2 G1_shift_l3_n3000 shd and J1 G6_weight_l0_n1000 target_error, 2e-17 in the confirmation's a1e-05_lexicographic_s10 G2_perfect_l1_n1000 shd), so those intervals touch 0 and the rows tie; the run's own scripts read them as above or below 0, which changed no decision. The same reading moves the first of them from above 0 to contains 0 in default_selection.trace.inv_n_sum_counts. Counts of single runs name sides (below 0, contains 0, above 0); better and worse name only comparisons that repeated | IGSP: an interval end within 1e-12 of 0, floating-point residue of an exact 0, is read as 0, as the UT-IGSP lane reads it; residue lists every such end, on seeds 0-19 unless it names a rerun's seeds, and side_as_computed fields give the side where the reading changes it. The gate and the confirmation's scripts read the ends as computed, under which four verdicts differ: the W row (J1 alpha 1e-4 patched) is above 0 on seeds 0-19 and again on seeds 100-119, a replicated worse row, where read exactly it ties; the two Y8 inhibiting n 1,000 rows at alpha 1e-2 against the patched copy are lower with no rerun instead of tied; Y8 inhibiting n 10,000 at alpha 1e-3 with 10 starts against the library is below 0 on seeds 6000-6019, so better (11, not 10); and the confirmation counts 18 rows below 0 for alpha 1e-3 against 17, keeping 1e-3, where read exactly the two tie at 17 and the rule, written before any fit, gives the tie to one over the observational rows, the default. Here interval ends are rounded to 4 decimals except those residue ends, which stay as computed, so above_zero reads them as computed, as qa/reference_parity.py does, while side and verdict read them as 0

differences.500_steps: in claim, 34 of the 280 paired series end on a different graph; CausalNex on centered columns (fitted on those 34 alone) returns Andrey's graph on 29. Of the other 5, Andrey's graph changes on 4 when the data are multiplied by 1 + 1e-12 noise or the columns are fitted in their given order. methods.same_graph_test: the same directed edges and the same marked pairs
methods.error_metric: direct_errors: the directed edges claimed against the edges between observed variables that no unobserved causal or backdoor path joins, the edges CAM-UV can identify as direct; a missing or extra edge costs 1 and a reversed one 2. shd_endpoint: the endpoint SHD against the PAG of the observed variables. shd_endpoint_bidirected: the same with the estimate's marked pairs drawn <->, the references' mark (Andrey draws o-o), so the two packages' graphs are compared without the mark convention. pair_precision and pair_recall: the marked pairs against the pairs an unobserved causal or backdoor path joins, pooled over the datasets of a cell. same_graph: the same directed edges and the same marked pairs, whatever the mark; same_marks: the same endpoint marks. The paper (Sect. 5) scores directed edges against another truth, x_j -> x_i wherever a directed path from x_j to x_i has no other observed variable on it, which also holds the pairs joined through a hidden intermediate and the direct edges a hidden common cause confounds; latent_projection_errors count the directed edges against it, a missing or extra edge 1 and a reversed one 2, and latent_projection_precision, _recall, and _f1, the paper's three scores, are means over the datasets of a cell; the verdict does not read them

The paper (Sect. 5) scores directed edges against another truth, x_j -> x_i wherever a directed path from x_j to x_i has no other observed variable on it, which also holds the pairs joined through a hidden intermediate and the direct edges a hidden common cause confounds; latent_projection_errors count the directed edges against it, a missing or extra edge 1 and a reversed one 2, and latent_projection_precision, _recall, and _f1, the paper's three scores, are means over the datasets of a cell; the verdict does not read them
